text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The University of Malawi's vice chancellor, Brown Chimphamba, told a graduation ceremony that laws governing the institution should be revamped to remove its archaic practices.
- Malawi's Jack Mapanje, based in Britain, said the country's writers and publishers could not be free unless the government repeals the censorship act.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party's president Gwanda Chakuamba, who last week succeeded Kamuzu Banda, said he would like to merge his party with the opposition Alliance For Democracy and urged those who opposed the move to resign.
